brains.name: Central Complex
brains.blurb: The central complex is the fly's navigation and steering centre: it keeps track of heading and turns it into steering commands. Its plasticity gate is driven by 123 neuromodulatory cells — dopamine, serotonin and octopamine — over 793 real synapses, and what they write into the fast weight fades within about two frames.
brains.label: CentralComplex_Pong v1
brains.strength: In 20 games to 11 against each scripted player: 11–9 against a noisy scripted player like the one it learned from (point share 0.52, returning 88.2% of its shots), 20–0 against a weaker one, and 0–20 against a perfect one.
brains.intro: The central complex is the fly's navigation and steering centre: it holds a compass-like heading signal and turns it into steering commands. Its cells are drawn on the atlas in four classes:
brains.note: In a real Drosophila this circuit tracks heading and steers. Here the same wiring steers a Pong paddle: six numbers (ball position and velocity, both paddle positions) drive the ring (ER, ExR) and PFN input neurons, the circuit takes one timestep per frame at 60 frames per second, and the paddle command (stay, up or down) is read from the voltage of the 50 PFL output neurons only. There is no dopamine gate. The state is carried through the whole game and never reset.
brains.rate_note: The input classes are driven by the game every frame; the paddle command is read from the PFL output neurons only.

cells.title: Ring neurons (ER, ExR)
cells.desc: Carry landmark and visual cues into the ellipsoid body. Here they receive the game input.

cells.title: PFN columnar neurons
cells.desc: Bring self-motion signals through the noduli into the fan-shaped body. Also driven by the game input.

cells.title: PFL output neurons
cells.desc: Steering outputs towards the lateral accessory lobe. The paddle readout sees only their membrane voltage.

cells.title: Other central-complex neurons
cells.desc: EPG heading cells, PEN, PEG, Delta and fan-shaped-body neurons: the circuit between input and output.

brains.name: Antennal Lobe
brains.blurb: The antennal lobe is the fly's first olfactory relay: it separates and sharpens smells. Its gate is octopaminergic — 2 cells over 703 real synapses, as the antennal lobe has no dopaminergic neurons — and what they write into the fast weight fades within about two frames.
brains.label: AntennalLobe_Pong v1
brains.strength: In 20 games to 11 against each scripted player: 20–0 against a noisy scripted player like the one it learned from (point share 0.74, returning 95.2% of its shots), 20–0 against a weaker one, and 0–20 against a perfect one.
brains.intro: The antennal lobe is the first relay of the fly's sense of smell. Its cells fall into three classes, all drawn on the atlas:
brains.note: In a real Drosophila receptor neurons from the antenna sort odours into glomeruli, local neurons mix and normalise them, and projection neurons send the result on. Here the same wiring steers a Pong paddle: six numbers (ball position and velocity, both paddle positions) drive the 2,730 receptor neurons, the circuit takes one timestep per frame at 60 frames per second, and the paddle command is read from the voltage of the 700 projection neurons only. There is no dopamine gate. The state is carried through the whole game and never reset.
brains.rate_note: The receptor neurons are driven by the game every frame; the paddle command is read from the projection neurons only.

cells.title: Receptor neurons (ORN, TRN, HRN)
cells.desc: Olfactory, thermo- and hygrosensory neurons from the antenna. Here they receive the game input.

cells.title: Projection neurons
cells.desc: Carry the glomerular code on to the mushroom body and lateral horn. The paddle readout sees only their membrane voltage.

cells.title: Local and interneurons
cells.desc: Mostly inhibitory local neurons that shape and normalise the code across glomeruli.

brains.name: Mushroom Body
brains.blurb: The mushroom body is the fly's centre for associative learning and memory. Its gate is dopaminergic — 340 dopaminergic neurons over 3,160 real synapses — and what they write into the fast weight fades within about a frame and a half.
brains.label: MushroomBody_Pong v1
brains.strength: In 20 games to 11 against each scripted player: 10–10 against a noisy scripted player like the one it learned from (point share 0.51, returning 87.0% of its shots), 20–0 against a weaker one, and 0–20 against a perfect one.
